Computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates significant intertextual connections within Pali literature. The narrative is heavily cited and expounded upon in its commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (146 matches, spanning up to segment §8.4–31.4), with additional commentary parallels detected in the *Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Petavatthu* itself, formulaic verses and narrative segments are shared with several other stories, including the *Saṁsāramocakapetivatthu* (Pv 13, §16.4–19.3), the *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31, §2.1–2.4), the *Nandāpetivatthu* (Pv 16, §11.6–12.2), and the *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus identifies low-scoring algorithmic alignments with the Tibetan canonical translation of the *Karmaśataka* (D0340) and another Tibetan Kanjur text [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
